s1.syndrome_frame: Congenital brain anomaly with ocular involvement
salient_findings: Severe thinning of frontal, parietal, and occipital lobes
key_facts: Born at 35 weeks 4 days’ gestation
Monochorionic diamniotic twins
Identical twin died in utero at 24 weeks
Fetal ultrasound showed microcephaly and ventricular enlargement
Postnatal MRI revealed microcephaly and ventricular enlargement
No intracranial hematoma or neoplastic lesions
Family history was noncontributory
Weak light reflexes bilaterally at 1 week of age
Mild optic nerve pallor
Fundus had a faint reddish tone
Retinal vessels appeared normal in caliber

shortlist.label: Walker-Warburg syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by congenital muscular dystrophy, brain malformations, and eye abnormalities, matching the case's microcephaly, ventricular enlargement, and ocular involvement

shortlist.label: Muscle-eye-brain disease
shortlist.why_kept: Involves congenital muscular dystrophy, brain malformations, and eye abnormalities, consistent with the case's presentation of microcephaly, ventricular enlargement, and weak light reflexes

shortlist.label: Fukuyama congenital muscular dystrophy
shortlist.why_kept: Presents with congenital muscular dystrophy, brain malformations, and possible ocular involvement, aligning with the case's findings of microcephaly and ventricular enlargement

shortlist.label: Dandy-Walker malformation
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by congenital brain anomaly with ventricular enlargement, which is consistent with the case's postnatal MRI findings

shortlist.label: Lissencephaly
shortlist.why_kept: Involves brain malformation with possible ocular involvement, and the case's MRI showing severe thinning of the frontal, parietal, and occipital lobes suggests a lissencephaly-like condition

raw.rationale: The combination of microcephaly, ventricular enlargement, and ocular abnormalities such as weak light reflexes and mild optic nerve pallor are consistent with Muscle-eye-brain disease, which is a congenital muscular dystrophy associated with brain and eye malformations.

rejected.label: Walker-Warburg syndrome
rejected.why: While it shares some similarities, Walker-Warburg syndrome typically presents with more severe ocular and muscular findings, and often with additional systemic anomalies.

rejected.label: Fukuyama congenital muscular dystrophy
rejected.why: Fukuyama congenital muscular dystrophy primarily affects the muscles and brain, with less emphasis on ocular findings compared to this case.

rejected.label: Dandy-Walker malformation
rejected.why: Dandy-Walker malformation is characterized by cerebellar hypoplasia and hydrocephalus, which are not the primary features in this case.

rejected.label: Lissencephaly
rejected.why: Lissencephaly is characterized by a smooth brain surface due to defective neuronal migration, which is not described in the provided imaging findings.
